name: Light Sage
lede: Light Sage is a pale yellowish green recorded only in the 2010 xkcd color survey, close enough to two ISCC-NBS names to count as near-duplicates.

sections.title: A light build of sage
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[light-grey-green]], [[granny-smith-apple]], [[very-light-green]] and [[very-light-green]], at 2.5, 3.1, 4.2 and 4.5 ΔE [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as very light yellowish green, about 2.8 units from that block's center [1]. Its Munsell notation is 9.3GY 8.8/5.1 and its LCH values are lightness 89, chroma 38, hue 136 degrees [1]. In sRGB its components run 188 red, 236 green and 172 blue, a pale mix where green leads but neither red nor blue falls far behind [1].

Two ISCC-NBS block names, Light Nile Green and Pale Nile Green, cluster close to this swatch [2]. See [[sage]] for the darker, greyer herb color this name lightens. [[olive]] sits further along the same yellow-green family, at a much lower lightness [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Within CIEDE2000 4, Light Sage appears in just 1 of our 23,781 archive paintings, rarer than 86% of our named colors, as photographed [3]. That single match is Alexander von Kotzebue's 1857 painting, where our within-painting lens also finds it as present [3].
